Control your [MPD](https://www.musicpd.org) players from Gladys: a Raspberry Pi
plugged into an amplifier with moOde, Volumio, piCorePlayer, or MPD itself.
Play, pause, change the song and the volume, start a playlist, play a doorbell
sound or a web radio and then go back to the music, see what is playing on the
dashboard. Everything stays on your local network: no cloud, no account.

> **Developed without the hardware: feedback welcome.** The integration was
> built and tested against a real MPD 0.24 running in Docker (without a sound
> card) and a simulated server, not on a moOde, Volumio or piCorePlayer
> player. Please report what works and what does not in the
> [issues](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mpd/issues).

This integration is not affiliated with the MPD project, nor with moOde,
Volumio or piCorePlayer.

## What you need

- Gladys Assistant **5.3.0** or later.
- For the search, browse and queue panels of the **Music** box: MPD **0.21**
  or later (covers embedded in the files: **0.22**). moOde, Volumio 3 and
  recent distributions ship 0.23 or 0.24.
- A player running **MPD**, reachable from Gladys on the network, on its MPD
  port (**6600** by default). moOde and piCorePlayer (with its MPD extension)
  expose it out of the box; MPD itself listens on the network when
  `bind_to_address` is `any` or the IP of the machine in `mpd.conf`.
- The password of MPD if `mpd.conf` has a `password` line. It needs the
  `read`, `add` and `control` rights (`password "secret@read,add,control"`).
  Most players have no password.

## Set up

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**, then **Install from GitHub**, and enter
   `https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mpd` (or install **Music Player Daemon**
   from the catalog once it is listed).
2. In **Configuration**, enter the address of your player (`192.168.1.20`,
   `moode.home`, or `192.168.1.20:6601` for another port), its password if it
   has one, and a name (`Living room`). Up to three more players below.
3. Choose the **Language of the devices** (names of the features, messages)
   and, if you want, the **Notification volume**. Save.
4. Click **Test the connection**: one line per player, with the MPD version,
   what it is doing, its volume and its playlists.
5. Open the **Discover** tab and add the devices.

Use fixed IP addresses (a DHCP reservation in your router) or names your DNS
resolves: names ending in `.local` do not resolve inside the integration
container.

## The device of each player

Each player is one device. Gladys shows it as a music player: the **Music**
dashboard box (play, pause, previous, next, volume) and the **Talk on a
speaker** scene action work with it.

| Feature (English names) | What it does                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Play                    | Plays the queue (a paused song resumes where it was).                                      |
| Pause                   | Pauses.                                                                                    |
| Previous track          | Goes to the previous song.                                                                 |
| Next track              | Goes to the next song.                                                                     |
| Volume                  | 0 to 100 %, as MPD sees it. Absent value when MPD has no mixer (fixed volume).             |
| Playback state          | 0 paused, 1 playing, 2 stopped. Writing it pauses, plays or stops.                         |
| Title                   | The title of the song (the song announced by a web radio).                                 |
| Artist                  | Its artist.                                                                                |
| Album                   | Its album (the station of a web radio).                                                    |
| Artwork                 | The cover, shown by the Music box (see below).                                             |
| Duration                | In seconds; 0 for a web radio.                                                             |
| Position                | In seconds; writing it seeks in the song.                                                  |
| Shuffle                 | MPD's random play, on or off.                                                              |
| Repeat                  | Off, the whole queue, or the current song (MPD's repeat and single).                       |
| Playlist                | A list of the playlists saved in MPD: picking one replaces the queue with it and plays it. |
| Notification            | Receives an address to play, then puts back what was playing (see below).                  |

The list of playlists follows MPD: a playlist saved or deleted on the player
appears or disappears in the list.

## Gladys 5.3 music player

Since Gladys 5.3, the **Music** box of the dashboard is a real player, and MPD
fills all of it:

- the cover, the title, the artist and the album, a progress bar you can drag
  to seek, play and pause, previous, next, shuffle, repeat and the volume;
- the **queue** (list button): the songs of the MPD queue, the current one
  highlighted; a tap plays another one;
- **search and browse** (magnifier button): the search asks MPD for songs
  (any tag) and looks in the names of the artists, the albums and the
  playlists; browsing starts with **Folders** (the music directory of MPD),
  **Artists**, **Albums** and **Playlists**. A tap plays the item in place of
  the queue; the secondary gesture adds it after the current song or at the
  end of the queue. A folder, an artist or an album plays whole (500 songs at
  most).

The **Play music on a speaker** scene action of Gladys picks a playlist, an
album, an artist, a folder or a song in the same panel, and plays it when the
scene runs.

**A device added before version 1.1.0** keeps working as before, without the
new features: open the **Discover** tab of the integration and click
**Update** on the player (Gladys offers it because the features changed). The
new features are added; the existing ones keep their scenes and dashboards.
**Playback state** changes: it reads 2 instead of 0 when MPD is stopped, and it
is no longer kept in the history (Gladys keeps no history of music features).

Covers come from MPD: the picture embedded in the file first, else the cover
file of its folder (`cover.jpg`, `folder.png`…). MPD sends it as it is in the
file, often a scan of a few megabytes, and Gladys shows a cover of **300 KB at
most**: the integration makes a larger one smaller (a JPEG of 400 pixels at
most), up to 10 MB (see Limits).

MPD has **no mute**: no Mute button for an MPD player (setting the volume to 0
would lose the volume to come back to).

## Dashboard widget

Add the **MPD player** widget to a dashboard. In its settings, pick a player
(empty: the first one of the configuration). It shows:

- the **title** of the song and, below, the artist and the album (or the name
  of the web radio);
- the **volume** as a gauge;
- the state (playing, paused, stopped), the position in the queue, random and
  repeat;
- four buttons: **Previous**, **Play** or **Pause**, **Next** and
  **Options…**. Options… opens a form filled with the current values: the
  volume, a playlist to play, random play and repeat. Only what you change is
  sent.

The widget follows the player as it changes: it is refreshed within ten
seconds when a song starts, the volume moves or a playlist is saved. The **Music** box of Gladys 5.3
(above) is the full player; this widget adds the **Options…** form and has no
cover.

## Scenes

### Actions

The player is chosen among the devices of the integration.

- **Play an MPD playlist**: replaces the queue with a playlist saved in MPD,
  by its name (capitals and accents do not matter), and plays it. The number
  of songs queued can be used in the next actions of the scene. An unknown
  name fails the action with the list of the playlists. You can also choose a
  playlist from a list with the core action **Control a device**, on the
  **Playlist** feature.
- **Play an address on MPD**: plays an address — a web radio
  (`http://…`, `https://…`), a sound on a web server, or a file of the music
  library of MPD (`sounds/doorbell.mp3`) — at the volume you give (empty:
  unchanged). _Then_: **Resume the previous music** (the address plays once,
  then what was playing comes back, see below) or **Keep playing it
  (replaces the queue)**. The action fails when MPD cannot play the address.
- **Clear the MPD queue**: removes every song from the queue; the player
  stops.
- **MPD random play**: on, off, or toggle. The result (on or off) can be used
  in the next actions.
- **MPD repeat**: off, the whole queue, or the current song.

### Notifications and "Talk on a speaker"

The **Notification** feature of a player, the **Play an address on MPD** action
with _Resume the previous music_, and the **Talk on a speaker** action of
Gladys (the voice comes from Gladys Plus) all work the same way:

1. the address is added at the end of the queue (your queue is never
   replaced) and played at once, with the **Notification volume** of the
   configuration (or the volume of the action);
2. MPD stops after it; it is then removed from the queue, and the volume and
   the options (random, repeat, single, consume) come back;
3. the song that was playing resumes at the second it was interrupted; a
   paused song stays paused, a stopped player stays stopped.

A second notification while the first one plays replaces it. If someone takes
over the player meanwhile (another song, the next one), the notification ends
without touching the music. A notification that still plays after five
minutes is ended and the music comes back. A web radio sent as a notification
is not a notification: it keeps playing (its address stays in the queue).

The **Talk on a speaker** action has a volume slider, but Gladys does not pass
it on to external integrations: use the **Notification volume** of the
configuration.

### Scene ideas

- **Doorbell**: when the doorbell button is pressed, _Play an address on MPD_
  `sounds/doorbell.mp3` on the living room player, volume 70, then resume the
  previous music.
- **Wake-up radio**: at 7:00 on weekdays, _Play an address on MPD_ with the
  address of your favorite radio, _Keep playing it_, volume 25; at 7:45, the
  **Pause** feature.
- **Nobody home**: when the house becomes empty, the **Pause** feature of
  every player.
- **Music follows the light**: when the **Playback state** of the living room
  player becomes 1 after sunset, turn on the living room lamps.
- **Evening**: at sunset, _Play an MPD playlist_ "Apéro", then _MPD random
  play_ on.

## How it refreshes

The integration keeps one connection open to each player and waits for its
changes (the MPD `idle` command): what happens on the player, from Gladys or
from another app, is in Gladys within a second. On top of that, every player
is read every 30 seconds (it also checks that the player still answers). Only
the changes are sent to Gladys; the position in the song only when it jumps
(Gladys moves the progress bar itself).

A player that stops answering is shown unreachable (transport badge of the
device, connection status of the integration), and the integration tries
again: after 2, 5, 15, 30 seconds, then every minute. Nothing else is needed
when it comes back.

MPD has no quota: the integration sends a few commands per change and two
every 30 seconds, on one connection per player.

## Troubleshooting

- **"MPD answered with too much at once"** in the music panel: a folder or a
  list larger than the integration reads (4 MB of text): open a smaller
  folder, or search.
- **"does not answer"**: check the address and the port (6600, or the one of
  `port` in `mpd.conf`), that MPD listens on the network (`bind_to_address`)
  and that no firewall blocks the port between Gladys and the player.
- **"password refused"** or **"a password is needed"**: enter the password of
  the `password` line of `mpd.conf`; it needs the `read`, `add` and `control`
  rights.
- **"no MPD server at this address and port"**: something else answers on
  this port (a web interface, for example): MPD listens on 6600 by default.
- **The volume stays empty**: MPD has no mixer (`mixer_type "none"` in moOde
  for a fixed-volume DAC, for example): change the volume on the amplifier.
- **A notification does not play**: the address must be reachable from the
  player itself (not from Gladys), in a format MPD can decode; a file of the
  library is given by its path in the library. **Test the connection** and
  the logs of the integration say why MPD refused it.
- **The Playlist list is empty**: MPD has no `playlist_directory`, or no
  playlist saved yet.
- **More details**: the logs of the integration (Integrations → Music Player
  Daemon → Logs) show the connections, the losses and the returns, and one
  line per command. Restart the container with `LOG_LEVEL=debug` to see every
  change received and every reading. Passwords are never written.

## Limits

- Up to four players. A player is known by its slot in the configuration:
  changing its address keeps the device and its history.
- Covers above 10 MB or 25 megapixels are not shown, nor covers in another
  format than JPEG, PNG and WebP (GIF…), nor WebP covers above 300 KB: the
  integration only reduces JPEG and PNG.
- The search of MPD ignores capitals; accents only when MPD was built with
  ICU (`café` may not find `Café` otherwise).
- No mute (MPD has none).
- No grouping of players (Snapcast) nor choice of outputs.
- MPD cannot be found automatically on the network: enter the addresses.
- The volume of the **Talk on a speaker** action is not passed on by Gladys
  (the **Notification volume** applies).
- Gladys 5.3.0 or later (the music player and its panels).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Music Player Daemon asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your MPD players | `section` | No | Any Music Player Daemon: a Raspberry Pi with moOde, Volumio, piCorePlayer, or MPD itself. Enter its IP address (port 6600 by default, add :port otherwise) and the password of mpd.conf if there is one. Up to four players. |
| Player address | `string` | No | IP address or name of the player, with :port if MPD does not listen on 6600. |
| Password | `secret` | No | The password line of mpd.conf. Empty if MPD has none (the usual case). |
| Name | `string` | No | Name of the device in Gladys. Empty: "MPD" followed by the address. |
| Second player | `section` | No | Same fields, for another MPD player of your network. |
| Player address | `string` | No |  |
| Password | `secret` | No |  |
| Name | `string` | No |  |
| Third player | `section` | No | Same fields, for another MPD player of your network. |
| Player address | `string` | No |  |
| Password | `secret` | No |  |
| Name | `string` | No |  |
| Fourth player | `section` | No | Same fields, for another MPD player of your network. |
| Player address | `string` | No |  |
| Password | `secret` | No |  |
| Name | `string` | No |  |
| Options | `section` | No | The notification of a player plays an address (a doorbell sound, an announcement), then puts back what was playing. |
| Notification volume | `select` | No | Volume during a notification, back to the previous one after. Gladys does not pass on the volume of its "Talk on a speaker" action. |
| Language of the devices | `select` | No | Names given to the features when a device is added (Volume, Playlist…), and language of the messages. |

## How to install Music Player Daemon in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Music Player Daemon appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-mpd:1.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mpd](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-mpd).

Music Player Daemon requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.
